items.title: REST APIs built for production use.
items.description: Owned five production REST APIs and contributed to more than 40. Built and maintained request validation, authentication, PostgreSQL data access, integrations and production support.

items.title: An agent that can use tools with permission.
items.description: Built a Node.js agentic AI system end to end. It supports tool calling, planning, multi-step execution, subagents, conversation state, structured outputs, streaming and human approval for changes. Added role-based authorization and audit logging. Built a provider-agnostic service for OpenAI, Gemini and Groq, with fallback, retries and rate-limit handling. Caching and API/LLM tuning cut typical runs from 30 - 60 seconds to 6 - 18 seconds.

items.title: Async workflows built to handle failures.
items.description: Used Redis, Bull, AWS SQS, Lambda and API Gateway for asynchronous processing, retries, caching and TTL-based work. Debugged production failures with CloudWatch and application logs. Improved an HTML personalization pipeline for 10K - 35K character pages from 30 - 50 seconds to 6 - 12 seconds.

sections.label: AFTER HOURS
sections.heading: A job scheduler I built from scratch.
sections.lead: A separate project for learning how distributed jobs behave under failure.
sections.description: It runs immediate, delayed and cron jobs across any number of workers with at-least-once delivery. PostgreSQL is the source of truth, with a transactional outbox feeding Redis Streams. Workers hold leases with heartbeats and fencing tokens, crashed jobs are reclaimed, and failures back off with jitter into a dead letter queue. It ships with priority lanes, rate limiting, backpressure, Prometheus metrics and a Grafana dashboard.

sections.label: SIDE QUESTS
sections.heading: Apps I've shipped beyond production work.

items.title: Perforvisor
items.description: An AI advisor on open-weight models that reads public reviews (Google Maps via SerpApi), builds a knowledge graph and answers business owners and consumers with cited evidence. Hybrid retrieval and review trends run on Tiger Data Postgres (pgvector + TimescaleDB). The live demo is offline for now: I stopped the GCP GPU that served the models because of hosting cost.
items.achievement: Winner · Best Use of Tiger Data · DEV Hacktoberfest Challenge 2

items.title: Medication Safety Graph
items.description: Built for Graph Hacks. Two agents walk a FalkorDB knowledge graph to flag medicine conflicts for caregivers, show the graph path behind every warning, name who to call and remember each clinician's decision for the next session.

items.title: EchoNote
items.description: A local-first voice-to-action desktop assistant. Press a shortcut, speak, and Gemma 4 turns the thought into a task, reminder, idea or note. Fully offline after setup, packaged as RPM, DEB and AppImage.

items.title: Creative Detour
items.description: An Android app that finds free moments between steps, screen time and calendar events and nudges you off your phone. Nudges are written by Gemma 4 running on the device. No account, no server.

items.title: PostPilot
items.description: A multi-agent Telegram bot that drafts daily posts per platform. A strategist, writer and critic loop over a Postgres-backed queue with RAG over each user's notes, checkpointed runs and shared daily quotas so it runs free.

items.title: Huntboard
items.description: A local-first desktop app for job searching. It collects openings from job boards, deduplicates and ranks them against your real experience, tailors your résumé without inventing anything and tracks every application.

items.title: Distributed Job Scheduler
items.description: Immediate, delayed and cron jobs with at-least-once delivery, a transactional outbox, fencing tokens, dead letter replay, priority lanes, rate limiting and Prometheus and Grafana observability.

items.title: KragDB
items.description: Building a database system from scratch to learn about storage, data management and database internals.
items.note: Learning from the storage layer up.

items.title: Open-source contributions
items.description: Merged fixes upstream: stabilized the queue panel hint in Breakscale's system design simulator to stop layout shifts, and fixed a failing new-service test phase in Stockroom.

items.title: CodePlaneAI
items.description: An orchestration service that turns a plain-English or Slack trigger into a structured plan, hands it to a coding agent, validates the result against protected-path policy, then branches, commits, pushes and opens a PR.
items.note: From a message to a pull request.

items.title: Campus Launch Desk
items.description: My Global Hack Week: Hacktoberfest challenges in one repo: a tested Campus Week Board mini app, one prompt benchmarked across Grok 4.7, Composer 2.5 and Gemini 4, and a two-bot Grok launch relay.
